title: Dutch baby
summary: A big oven pancake that puffs in a hot skillet and settles into a custardy centre, served with lemon and powdered sweetener.
steps: Put a 25 cm (10 in) cast-iron or ovenproof skillet in the oven and heat to 220 °C (425 °F).
Blend the eggs, milk, almond flour, coconut flour, erythritol, vanilla and salt until smooth and frothy, about 1 minute.
Take the hot skillet out, add the butter and swirl until melted and foaming. Pour in the batter at once.
Bake 15–18 minutes without opening the door, until puffed and well browned at the edge.
Squeeze lemon juice over, dust with powdered erythritol and cut into wedges straight away; it sinks as it cools.
dairy_free_notes: Without gluten it rises less than a wheat Dutch baby — expect puffed edges and a flatter, custardy middle. The dairy-free version browns a little less.
tips: A very hot pan matters more than anything; do not skip preheating it.

origin.history: The Dutch baby is an American dish adapted from German oven pancakes; "Dutch" is generally taken as a corruption of Deutsch. It is often credited to a Seattle family café in the early 1900s, where the name is said to have been coined.
